toc.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence; ML: machine learning; LLM: large language model; RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation; MCP: Model Context Protocol; CLI: command-line interface; GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation; HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act; FedRAMP: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program; BAA: business associate agreement; ZDR: zero data retention

  • What the exam is: 63 items, 120 minutes, a scaled score of 720 to pass
  • The seven domains, their weights and the 38 objectives behind them
  • The minimally qualified candidate the exam is written for
  • The architect decision rules that explain most correct answers
  • How the course is built and how to use it

Who this exam is for. A mid- to senior-level practitioner (solution architect, AI/ML engineer, technical lead, senior engineer) who designs, builds and delivers production-grade Claude solutions: choosing models and patterns, engineering prompts and context, integrating with enterprise systems, and building in evaluation, security, compliance and governance. It is not for entry-level developers or casual users.

2The Exam at a Glance

Fact Value (guide v1.0, July 2026)
Credential / code Claude Architect – Professional / CCAR-P
Items 63, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select
Time 120 minutes (about 1 minute 54 seconds per item)
Passing score 720 on a scaled range of 100 to 1,000 (criterion-referenced: a fixed standard, not a ranking)
Fee USD 175 per attempt [Verify live]
Delivery Proctored by Pearson VUE: online or at a test center
Validity 12 months from the date the credential is awarded; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment
Retakes Wait 14 days after the first failed attempt, 30 after the second, 90 after the third; at most 4 attempts in a rolling 12 months; limits are per exam
Prerequisites None are required; recommended: 3+ years in systems architecture or platform engineering and 6+ months with Claude or comparable LLM systems in production
Score report Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (domain figures do not decide pass or fail)
Exam tip

For a multiple-response item the stem says how many answers to select: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

3The Seven Domains

Domain Weight What it asks you to do Modules
D3 Integration 19% Spot tool bloat and security gaps; trade accuracy against latency; design RAG; choose MCP, API/CLI or agent-to-agent; observe at scale 7 to 10
D1 Solution Design & Architecture 17% Turn business problems into architectures; pick workflow, agentic or augmented-LLM patterns; design multi-agent systems; decompose 1 to 3
D4 Evaluation, Testing & Optimization 16% Define metrics and datasets; A/B test; diagnose; optimize cost, latency, tokens; monitor 11, 12
D5 Governance, Safety & Risk 14% Guardrails, failure modes, human review, GDPR, HIPAA, FedRAMP, ethics 13, 14
D6 Stakeholder Communication & Lifecycle 14% Discovery, communicating trade-offs, SLAs, documentation, lifecycle phases 15, 16
D2 Claude Models, Prompting & Context 13% Model trade-offs, system prompts, prompting techniques, context and token management, reuse 4 to 6
D7 Developer Productivity & Operational Enablement 7% Configure Claude Code for teams, AI-assisted workflows, debugging and operations 17
  • Of 63 items, about 12 come from D3, 11 from D1, 10 from D4, 9 each from D5 and D6, 8 from D2 and 4 to 5 from D7.
  • Weights are the approximate share of scored items. Items are written against the 38 objectives listed in the guide.
  • Study order by value: D3 and D1 first (over a third together), then D4, D5, D6 and D2; D7 is the smallest.
Exam tip

No domain is negligible except D7 at 7 percent. Integration is the largest, so give it the most practice.

4The Minimally Qualified Candidate

Running case

Lumen Advisory

  • Throughout the course you follow Lumen Advisory, a fictional consultancy
  • Its architects design Claude solutions for clients in banking, healthcare, retail and government
  • Each module solves one architecture problem for a client; the questions use the same style as the exam

The minimally qualified candidate (MQC) can:

  • translate business requirements into scalable, secure, reliable architectures
  • design end-to-end systems: prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), API integration, orchestration and evaluation
  • weigh trade-offs among cost, latency, performance, safety and maintainability
  • integrate Claude into production systems with APIs, orchestration tools and data pipelines
  • build in evaluation, monitoring, security, compliance and governance
  • communicate architectural decisions to engineers, legal and executives

5Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

Most items describe a requirement or a failure and ask for the best design choice. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Each later module shows them at work.

# Rule Typical wrong answers
1 Start with the simplest pattern that meets the need (single call, then workflow, then agent) An agent or multi-agent system for a fixed task
2 Remove risk at the source: least privilege means removing capabilities, not logging them Adding logging or a confirmation instead of removing the tool
3 Cache the stable prefix; put static content before dynamic content Truncating needed context or shrinking the model blindly
4 Match the model to the task and prove it with evals "Always the largest" or "always the smallest"
5 Retrieve only what is needed: tool search, progressive discovery, RAG for large knowledge, full context for small Loading every tool and document up front
6 Investigate the first place the symptom points: confident wrong answers after a refresh point to retrieval Blaming silent model changes
7 Measure before and after with defined metrics, datasets and controlled comparisons Judging by a few impressions
8 Keep humans in the loop for irreversible or high-risk actions, and enforce rules in code Stronger prompt wording
9 Meet the regime with the right platform and contract (BAA, ZDR, data residency, GovCloud) Assuming any API route is compliant
10 Communicate trade-offs, assumptions and SLAs and document decisions Promising certainty or hiding limits
Exam tip

When two options both work, prefer the one that is simple, least-privileged, measured, cost-aware and compliant.

6How to Use This Course

  • Order: read modules 1 to 17 in order (they follow the domains), then module 18 (recap) and 19 (technique).
  • Each module has the objectives it covers, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, scenario questions with explanations and a Quick Reference Card.
  • Build one end-to-end solution. The guide recommends building and operating at least one Claude solution with RAG, evaluation and observability.
  • Product details change fast. Boxes marked [Verify live] show current behavior. On the exam, answer by the principle and check the official documentation for current details.
  • Independence. This course is independent study material; it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic or Pearson VUE. Read the official exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Exam Policy before you register.

7Exam Q&A

S1A senior engineer with five years of experience asks whether a prior Claude credential is required to sit the exam. What is the answer?

  • ANo: there are no mandatory prerequisites, although architecture and Claude production experience are recommended
  • BYes: the Associate and Developer credentials must be held first and renewed every year
  • CYes: a completed partner training course is required before the exam can be scheduled
  • DYes: three years of formal certification history with the same vendor is mandatory
Show the answer

Answer: A. The guide requires nothing and awards the credential on exam performance alone.

S2Which domain carries the largest share of the scored items?

  • ASolution Design & Architecture
  • BIntegration
  • CDeveloper Productivity & Operational Enablement
  • DEvaluation, Testing & Optimization
Show the answer

Answer: B. Integration is 19%, the largest of the seven domains.

S3A candidate scores 710 overall but 95 percent in one domain. What is the result?

  • APass, because domain percentages are averaged into the result
  • BFail, because each domain must also reach 720 separately
  • CFail, because the total scaled score is below 720
  • DPass, because one very strong domain compensates for the rest
Show the answer

Answer: C. The pass decision uses only the total scaled score; domain percentages are reported for guidance.

S4Which person is the exam written for?

  • AA casual user who writes prompts in a chat application for personal tasks
  • BAn entry-level developer who has just completed a first tutorial on the API
  • CA manager who approves budgets for AI tools but takes no part in the design of the system itself
  • DA technical professional who designs and delivers production Claude solutions end to end
Show the answer

Answer: D. The audience is experienced architects and senior engineers; entry-level developers and casual users are excluded.

8Quick Reference Card

Domains D3 19 · D1 17 · D4 16 · D5 14 · D6 14 · D2 13 · D7 7
